chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd, who linked it up to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him),

He said: The servant (person) continues to steal until, when the value of the blood money for his hand is fully paid (i.e., the theft reaches the threshold for cutting the hand), God makes it manifest (known).

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the servant/person (general term for a human being in this context)
key_terms.دِيَةِ يَدِهِ: blood money for his hand (referring to the threshold for hadd punishment)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for God revealing a thief's crime and leading to the cutting of the hand?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine mechanism of gradual concealment (istidraj) regarding the punishment of theft, noting that God hides the sin as long as the stolen amount remains below the nisab for cutting the hand. Once the accumulated value reaches the full diya (blood money) of the hand, God reveals the thief's guilt, leading to the execution of the hudud punishment. This tradition highlights the precision of divine justice in tracking even minor transgressions until they reach a critical threshold.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-35 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd who linked it up to Abil Hassan Al-Ridha (s), “

God will not divulge the theft of a servant (someone) for as long as his penalty is less than (the expiation for) his hand. However, if the expiation for the theft is as much as (the expiation for) the thief’s hand, then God will make it known.”
